propose: The official TIDMAD paper (Fry et al., arXiv:2406.04378v3, Appendix B) reports an FC Net autoencoder for 40,000-sample input windows. Its encoder is Linear(40000, 4000, bias=True), ReLU, Linear(4000, 400, bias=True), ReLU, Linear(400, 40, bias=True). Its decoder is Linear(40, 400, bias=True), ReLU, Linear(400, 4000, bias=True), ReLU, Linear(4000, 40000, bias=True). There is no reported activation after the 40-dimensional bottleneck or the final output layer. This is approximately 323 million trainable parameters from the listed layers. The paper trains this continuous-output model with MSE; this experiment does not require that loss.

Consider encoder-decoder designs that compress and reconstruct long waveform windows, including but not limited to the reported FC Net. The architecture and loss remain choices to test against the declared score and Health checks; do not treat the reference model as a required implementation.

RNN or recurrent seq2seq designs are allowed, but they are not a preferred starting point for 40,000-sample windows because sequential recurrence can make training and inference too slow for this experiment's budgets. Reconsider them if measured evidence justifies their cost.

The declared workflow has up to 100 iterations and 3 rounds per iteration. Trial and Formal each have a 40-GiB VRAM ceiling and an epoch ceiling of 2. The Trial time-admission budget is 30 minutes and the Formal time-admission budget is 120 minutes; these are planning and admission budgets, not guarantees of time available to a model. The independent run-wide wall-clock limit is 24 hours. The agent chooses Trial and Formal training strategy and portions from the selected band's training files, and chooses the Trial validation portion. Formal evaluation scores the complete validation band, regardless of training portion, and supplies the official comparable score. Use observed timing, GPU memory, score, and Health feedback when choosing model size, training strategy, and training work.
tune: Plan Trial and Formal training within their declared 40-GiB VRAM, 2-epoch, and 30/120-minute time-admission budgets. Compare proposed epochs with the epochs and measured training time of earlier attempts; do not assume a two-epoch run costs the same as a one-epoch run. Choose the loss, batch strategy, and model size from the observed evidence rather than treating the paper's FC Net or MSE as mandatory.
